questions.question: Differentiate briefly between recruitment and selection.
questions.solution_html:
• Recruitment is the process of searching for and encouraging potential candidates to apply, whereas
  • selection is the process of screening, evaluating, and hiring the best candidate.
  • Recruitment is a positive process because it aims to attract a large applicant pool, while selection is
  • considered a negative process because it involves rejecting unsuitable applicants. Recruitment
  • always precedes selection, whereas selection follows recruitment.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: always precedes selection, whereas selection follows recruitment.

questions.question: Define media as an industry.
questions.solution_html:
• The commercial ecosystem involved in the large-scale creation, production, aggregation
  • and distribution of information, news, and entertainment content. Operates on a dual

questions.question: Write a short essay examining the role of ratings and audience feedback in commercial media broadcasting.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of ratings and audience feedback in commercial media broadcasting.
  • Audience Measurement & Metrics: Television Rating Points (TRP) / Target Rating
  • Points, Listenership ratings (RAM), and digital metrics (views, click-through rates).
  • Revenue Generation: Ratings establish ad-rate cards; higher ratings directly attract
  • premium advertisers and sponsorships.
  • Programming & Content Decisions: Determines show renewals, time-slot adjustments
  • cancellations, and format refreshes based on viewer preferences.
  • Audience Feedback Integration:Social media comments, focus groups, and call-in
  • feedback aid in editorial alignment, crisis management, and viewer retention strategies.

questions.question: Write a short essay on how media managers distribute resources during breaking news.
questions.solution_html:
• Immediate Personnel Reallocation: Deployment of field reporters, camera crews, and
  • mobile news gatherers (DSNG/OB units) to the event site instantly.
  • Studio & Production Realignment: Overriding scheduled programming; reallocating
  • control rooms (PCR/MCR), anchors, and live graphics teams for continuous coverage.
  • Bandwidth & Technical Logistics: Securing satellite links, IP-cellular backpacks (LiveU)
  • and cloud editing pipelines for low-latency transmission.
  • Financial & Safety Emergency Buffers: Tapping into contingency budgets for crew
  • travel, emergency equipment rental, and field safety protocols.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: travel, emergency equipment rental, and field safety protocols.

questions.question: How does Gulāb Koṭhārī's framework in Newspaper Management in India combine standard management rules with the cultural and social needs of regional publishing?
questions.solution_html:
• Gulab Kothari's framework in Newspaper Management in India.
  • Harmonization of Management & Culture: Blends universal administrative principles
  • (Fayol/Taylor) with regional Indian socio-cultural dynamics.
  • Editorial Independence vs. Commercial Realities: Treats the newspaper not merely as a
  • profit center, but as a public trust carrying ethical responsibility toward society.
  • Regional Audience Centricity: Emphasizes hyper-local coverage, language nuances, and
  • traditional community values over westernized corporate models.
  • Operational Flexibility: Advocates for flexible organizational structures suited to regional
  • supply chain constraints, localized circulation networks, and regional ad-markets.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: supply chain constraints, localized circulation networks, and regional ad-markets.

questions.question: Examine the budgeting process and financial planning strategies unique to newspaper publishing.
questions.solution_html:
• Budgeting process and financial planning unique to newspaper publishing.
  • Revenue Stream Forecasting: Projecting dual revenue streams: Advertising income
  • (display, classifieds, government ads) and Circulation income (subscriptions, cover price
  • sales).
  • Cost Center Structure: First-Copy Costs (Fixed): Editorial salaries, news gathering
  • (wire services), photography, prepress, and administrative overheads.
  • Variable / Reproduction Costs: Newsprint paper stock (major expense driver), ink
  • printing machinery maintenance, electricity, and distribution commission.
  • Newsprint Cost Volatility Management: Buffering budgets against global paper price
  • fluctuations, import duties, and currency exchange rates.
  • Circulation & Yield Optimization: Calculating net paid circulation vs. unsold copies
  • (returns/waste paper realization).
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the core functions of media management within a publishing or broadcast organization.
questions.solution_html:
• Core functions of media management within a publishing or broadcast
  • organization.
  • • Planning: Setting editorial policies, long-term content strategies, broadcast grids, and
  • financial projections.
  • • Organizing: Structuring departments (editorial, production, sales, technical
  • marketing) and defining chains of command.
  • • Staffing & Human Resources: Recruiting specialized creative/technical talent
  • managing freelancer contracts, and handling shift rotas.
  • • Directing & Coordinating: Aligning daily workflows across newsrooms, studios
  • technical teams, and commercial departments.
  • • Controlling & Monitoring: Quality control, legal compliance, ratings tracking, audit
  • verification (e.g., ABC/RNI), and budgetary control.

questions.question: Write a comprehensive essay explaining the three phases of production management - pre-production, production, and post-production - highlighting the importance of workflow and coordination.
questions.solution_html:
• Three phases of production management: Pre-production, Production, and Post
  • production.
  • A. Pre-Production Phase (Planning & Preparation)
  • Concept Development: Scriptwriting, storyboarding, format finalization, and editorial
  • approvals.
  • Resource Scheduling & Budgeting: Allocating funds, securing permits, copyright
  • clearances, and talent hiring.
  • Logistics & Scouting: Location scouting, equipment checks, set design, and technical
  • rehearsal scheduling.
  • B. Production Phase (Execution & Capture)
  • Content Creation: Live broadcasting, principal photography, filming, and audio
  • recording.
  • On-Set Management: Coordinating director, floor manager, camera operators, sound
  • technicians, and talent/anchors.
  • Time & Quality Control: Adhering to call sheets, managing shot lists, and ensuring
  • technical standards (lighting, sound levels).
  • C. Post-Production Phase (Assembly & Delivery)
  • Editing & Assembly: Offline/online video editing, audio mixing/dubbing, color grading
  • and visual graphics/VFX addition.
  • Mastering & Quality Check: Technical compliance check (aspect ratios, broadcast
  • loudness standards, frame rates).
  • Archiving & Distribution: Encoding for multi-platform delivery (TV transmission, OTT
  • web) and metadata tagging for archives.
  • D. Workflow & Coordination Importance
  • • Prevents cost overruns, missing transmission deadlines, and technical errors.
  • • Ensures seamless inter-departmental handoffs from creative teams to technical
  • operators.
